scenes.say: Squinting at your phone? Do this, not that.

scenes.en: After about 40, the lens inside the eye gets stiffer. Near focus gets harder.
scenes.say: Here is why. After about forty, the lens inside your eye slowly gets stiffer, so focusing up close gets harder. This is natural, and it happens to almost everyone.

scenes.en: Increase font size and display zoom. Turn on bold text.
scenes.say: Do this. In your phone settings, increase the font size and display zoom, and turn on bold text.

scenes.en: Match brightness to the room. Hold the phone about an arm's length away.
scenes.say: Match screen brightness to the room light, and hold the phone a comfortable distance away.

scenes.en: Don't scroll in a dark room. Don't hold it close to your nose.
scenes.say: Do not scroll in a dark room, and do not hold the phone close to your nose. Every twenty minutes, look far away for twenty seconds.

scenes.en: If you push the phone farther away to read, you may need reading power.
scenes.say: Did you know? If you keep pushing the phone farther away to read, you may simply need reading glasses. Bigger fonts help, but they do not fix it.
